title: David choe's experience on baboon hunting
summary: A 2:09 clip titled as David Choe’s baboon-hunting experience. An unresolved primary storyteller describes difficult living conditions, homemade bows/arrows and plant poison, then makes racialized claims about black skin, cooling, sweating and endurance while recounting five hours of running and drinking a handful of brown water. He recalls unsuccessful hunts and a first recorded kill in graphic detail: dogs tear a baboon’s abdomen, the animal throws dogs and people enter its chest. The exchange then distinguishes tasting from eating before later admitting eating baboon meat; it was strong/gamey, prompted an explicitly speculative human-flesh analogy, and was linked by another probable voice to strength/testosterone. Every idea remains. Group, place, identities, censored words, physiology, cultural representativeness and causal explanations remain unverified; zero named turns and enrollment windows ship.
